deferredRules.reason: The policy edits that add "by default" to every high-assurance human-review sentence are built with the L3 goal (design decision D39); until then the default human rule is the rule, so the check is not active.

rows.quote: - `INVARIANT`: Never couple core SDLC logic to vendor-specific session formats or proprietary database engines.
rows.note: Neutral source and harness contracts isolate core behavior from source systems and vendor invocation formats.

rows.quote: - `MUST`: Distinguish between the **runtime platform slug** (who provided workflow evidence, e.g., `agy`, `claude`, `codex`, `pi`) and the **execution target**
rows.note: The target resolver separates platform identity from execution target, transport and delegation boundary.

rows.quote: - `MUST NOT`: Assume an agent executes in its own native environment or inherit providers implicitly.
rows.note: Ambiguous cross-agent requests require clarification rather than inheriting the current provider.

rows.quote: - `INVARIANT`: All completed role transitions produce tamper-evident, cryptographically chained records.
rows.note: Run events carry checked digests and parent links, with tests rejecting conflicting parents and tampered replay.

rows.quote: - `MUST`: Apply the review model in `AGENTS.md` and `docs/agent-workflow.md`: bounded work may use explicit, evidence-backed self-review; standard work may use
rows.note: Role-pass validation rejects high-assurance self-review and human gates reject agent reviewers, although signed human authentication remains future work.

rows.quote: - `MUST`: Enforce strict Separation of Duties. The `tester` and `reviewer` roles are strictly read-only (`observe` boundary) and must never repair or modify
rows.note: The QA contract helper does not contain executing agents, so full enforcement needs tester lane P-2 and reviewer lane M2-3.

rows.quote: - `INVARIANT`: Cards are categorized into explicit taxonomy profiles: `light`, `standard`, and `high-assurance`.
rows.note: The vocabulary defines light, standard and high-assurance profiles and the goal model derives the selected risk profile.

rows.quote: - `MUST`: Dynamically bypass non-applicable design or verification gates for `light` tasks (e.g., minor docs, non-functional tweaks) when project posture
rows.note: Optional role projection exists, but no inspected test proves the claimed dynamic design and verification gate bypass and no specific design item schedules that gap.

rows.quote: - `MUST`: Require multi-agent consensus, rigorous exploratory QA, and formal human security sign-off for `high-assurance` tasks.
rows.note: Review policy checks exist, but the independently contained cross-family reviewer lane is planned in M2-3 and signed human acts in M1-13.

rows.quote: - `MUST`: Enforce topological dependency ordering (`blocked_by`). A card cannot transition to implementation if prerequisite dependency cards remain unverified.
rows.note: The cockpit displays open dependency blockers, but no inspected transition guard proves that unverified prerequisites forbid implementation and no specific design item schedules it.

rows.quote: - `INVARIANT`: Transition gates must present concise, actionable decision context, highlighting residual risk, verification receipts, and test coverage gaps.
rows.note: The gate dialog presents risk, evidence readiness dimensions and missing-check context with rendering tests.

rows.quote: - `MUST NOT`: Force humans into repetitive, low-context approvals for deterministic, evidence-backed steps.
rows.note: This is an agent interaction instruction with no enforcing check for repetitive or low-context approvals.

rows.quote: - `MUST`: Require human justification and explicit logging whenever an automated gate or invariant is bypassed via an emergency waiver.
rows.note: Waiver checks require a reason and independent approver for high-assurance work and the transition comment records the justification.

rows.quote: - `INVARIANT`: Uncommitted work and pipeline state must never be trapped on a single physical machine.
rows.note: Portable run recovery does not preserve arbitrary uncommitted work remotely, and the design retracts automatic WIP checkpoints without scheduling a replacement for this universal claim.

rows.quote: - `MUST`: Keep run state in the run store, where each event carries a writer generation and the digest of the event before it, so that a stale writer cannot
rows.note: The reducer rejects stale parents and writer generations and resume advances the generation after confirmed writer termination.

rows.quote: - `MUST`: Normalize file paths to POSIX (`/`) and scrub credentials, API keys, and local PII before pushing state.
rows.note: Tested sanitization helpers redact engineering evidence, but universal scrubbing before state pushes has no inspected enforcing caller or specific scheduled design item.

rows.quote: - `INVARIANT (Zero Deadlock)`: Every asynchronous verification gate must deterministically resolve within a configured deadline (default: 30 minutes).
rows.note: The in-memory sweeper has deadline tests but its persisted state and first product caller are scheduled for M1-9.

rows.quote: - `MUST`: Employ a three-tier gate resolution architecture:
rows.note: Webhook, reconciliation and timeout helpers do not establish a running three-tier gate service until M1-9 wires the sweeper.

rows.quote: - `MUST`: Supervise all spawned child processes in monitored process trees, guaranteeing SIGTERM/SIGKILL termination and zero port lockups (`EADDRINUSE`).
rows.note: Some process-tree kill callers exist, but persisted supervisor registration and orphan reconciliation remain scheduled for P-3.

rows.quote: - `MUST`: Automatically extract external failure logs and inject them directly into downstream revision prompt loops.
rows.note: The sweeper collects external failure logs, but no product caller injects them into revision prompts and no specific design item schedules that missing loop.
